national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Sede Electrónica — https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. For mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands, AEAT administers corporate income tax, VAT (IVA), customs duties, and withholding taxes. The Basque Country and Navarra have separate provincial tax administrations for income taxes, while AEAT retains VAT and customs jurisdiction. For an ES_SL (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada), the applicable portals are the AEAT Sede Electrónica, the Registro Mercantil for corporate registration, and the Spanish Customs System (Sistema de Aduanas / DUA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Procedure for a foreign entity to obtain statutory TIN/VAT ID in Spain: (1) Determine Spanish tax nexus: a non-resident company with no permanent establishment and no local supplies may not require a Spanish income-tax NIF, but a Spanish VAT NIF is required for any taxable supply in Spain, intra-EU acquisitions, or import/customs operations. (2) If the foreign investor incorporates a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, the notary requests a provisional NIF certificate for the company from AEAT before registration at the Registro Mercantil, and the company must subsequently file Declaración Censal Form 036/037 to complete registration in the Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores. (3) For a non-resident entity without a permanent establishment, file Form 036 with the AEAT tax office for non-resident taxpayers, attaching certified constitutional deed, certificate of incorporation, tax residence certificate, passport/governing body identification, and evidence of the appointed representative. (4) Non-EU/EEA residents must appoint a tax representative resident in Spain with a NIF/NIE; the representative bears joint and several liability for penalties under Article 86 of Ley General Tributaria. (5) AEAT assigns a definitive NIF to legal entities in the format of a legal-form letter plus eight digits plus a control character. (6) For VAT purposes, the same NIF constitutes the Spanish NIF-IVA; intra-EU traders must be enrolled in the Censo de Operadores Intracomunitarios and use a VAT identification number formatted ESXXXXXXXXX. (7) Entities filing customs declarations must have an EORI number issued by Spanish Customs, may use a customs representative, and must register in the customs electronic system before undertaking export operations of sulfur mineral ores.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not operate a US-style check-the-box pass-through election for an SL. An ES_SL is a company subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades at entity level on worldwide income, with liability limited to its capital. Available statutory elections include: (i) reduced 15% corporate income tax rate for newly created companies in the first two taxable periods with positive net taxable income, under Article 29.3 Ley del Impuesto sobre Sociedades; (ii) election for tax consolidation regime for Spanish group members under Chapter VII LIS, requiring 80% direct or indirect control; (iii) election for the holding regime of Empresa de Tenencia de Valores Extranjeros (ETVE) for foreign shareholding; (iv) patent-box election (30% exemption on qualifying innovation income) under the OECD nexus approach; and (v) optional VAT simplified/cash-accounting regimes when annual turnover does not exceed EUR 100,000. Hybrid mismatch rules in Article 15a LIS are mandatory anti-avoidance rules under ATAD and cannot be neutralized by election; financial instrument classification is determined by legal substance.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA — Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (Value Added Tax) applicable in mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands; the Canary Islands are outside the EU VAT area and apply IGIC, while Ceuta and Melilla apply IPSI. The IVA is governed by Ley 37/1992 and implementing regulations, fully harmonized with the EU VAT Directive.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general annual VAT registration threshold in Spain; any taxable person carrying out an economic activity must file Form 036/037 and register before starting supplies. For the simplified regime, an annual turnover ceiling of EUR 100,000 applies; for intra-EU distance sales of goods, Spain applies the lower threshold of EUR 35,000. Import of goods into Spain, first intra-EU acquisition, or first taxable domestic supply each independently trigger VAT registration irrespective of annual turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not impose physical pre-clearance digital stamping of each invoice. It operates real-time electronic reporting through two complementary systems: (i) Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII), mandatory for taxpayers with annual turnover above EUR 6,010,121.04 and for all VAT groups, requiring submission of invoice records to AEAT via web services/API protocols within four calendar days following invoice issue or receipt; and (ii) Verifactu under Real Decreto 1007/2023, requiring certified billing software to generate a verification linkage and QR hash and to retain a standard XML invoice dataset accessible to AEAT, complemented by the B2B electronic invoicing mandate under Ley 18/2022 'Crea y Crece'. For a sulfur ore trading entity, AEAT will expect ERP/API integration and retention of complete invoice metadata, including buyer identity, Incoterms, customs codes, and payment evidence, for at least four years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The export of granular elemental sulfur to destinations outside the European Union qualifies for VAT zero-rating under Article 21 Ley 37/1992 if: (i) the seller is a taxable person acting as such and established in Spain; (ii) the goods are physically removed from the customs territory of the European Union within the legally required period, normally three months from delivery; (iii) the export is evidenced by a valid customs export declaration (DUA) accepted by Spanish Customs; (iv) transportation to the non-EU destination is direct and supported by a Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document; (v) the transaction is genuine, at arm's length, and the goods are exported by the seller or on its behalf; and (vi) the seller retains complete commercial and treasury documents. Directly related services, including loading, international transport, and freight forwarding, are typically exempt or zero-rated if properly substantiated. If the goods are diverted, re-introduced into the EU, or not exported within the permitted period, the zero-rating is denied.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration — Documento Único Administrativo (DUA/SAD), with accepted exportation status and Movement Reference Number (MRN) from Spanish Customs
Bill of Lading (B/L) or equivalent multimodal/sea waybill evidencing port loading and non-EU destination of the sulfur cargo
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT MT103/Letter-of-Credit settlement proof demonstrating payment of the export price in foreign currency
Commercial invoice issued in the name of the non-EU buyer, showing product description, ISIC 4669 trading scope, Incoterms, price, and HS classification of the sulfur ore
Packing list and official weight/quality certificate (shipper's/tallyman's certificate) for dry bulk cargo
Export carrier's delivery receipt, customs transit/exit confirmation, or AEAT electronic status proving physical departure from the EU
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT uses SII filings, customs declarations, port manifests, freight records, banking transfers, and cross-border information sharing to verify that zero-rated sulfur exports physically left the EU and that proceeds correspond to the declared transaction. If documentation is missing, false, or inconsistent, AEAT regularizes the supply, imposes the standard 21% IVA, plus late-payment interest, and applies penalties under Articles 191 and 193 LGT of 50% up to 150% of the tax base, increasing to 100%–150% where fraud is established. Failure to evidence inward remittance within the 180-day foreign-currency repatriation convention may be treated as a suspect export and trigger retrospective clawback of VAT refunds and internal revenue charges. Criminal tax fraud liability arises under Organic Law 10/1995 where defrauded IVA in any fiscal year exceeds EUR 120,000, with potential imprisonment and additional fines for customs documents falsification. The general Spanish tax statute of limitations for VAT assessments is four years, but delays, unreported facts, or criminal proceedings may extend the exposure window.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) as the national central bank and monetary authority; the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business (Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa) and its General Directorate of International Trade and Investments exercise foreign investment regulation; SEPBLAC (the Financial Intelligence Unit within the Bank of Spain) performs AML/CFT supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Euro is fully convertible within the euro area. Spain applies full capital and current account liberalisation under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Royal Decree 1816/1991, as amended. No prior exchange control authorisation is required for profit remittances, dividend distributions, or the repatriation of liquidation proceeds. Non-resident shareholders of Spanish SLs may freely remit dividends subject to withholding tax and corporate accounting verification. A statistical declaration to the Bank of Spain is required for external transactions exceeding €50,000 or where the cumulative foreign investment exceeds €3,000,000; this is administrative, not a substantively restrictive control.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory surrender or conversion requirement for export proceeds in Spain. Exporters may retain foreign currency balances, convert to euros at market rates, or use them for trade settlements. There is no statutory deadline for repatriation of export receipts. However, resident exporters must report all export collections through an authorised Spanish resident bank using the official declaration mechanisms for balance-of-payments and foreign-transaction statistical purposes; intra-EU exports are reported quarterly, non-EU exports monthly; all filings are channelled by the receiving bank to Banco de España.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium with significant legal constraints. PSD2-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) registered with Banco de España, such as Monei, N26, Revolut Business, and Openbank, can provide remote corporate accounts, SEPA payments, and multi-currency virtual IBANs. For an SL engaged in granular elemental sulfur dry-bulk trade, EMIs are viable for invoice receipts and low-value operational disbursements, but have limited utility for documentary credits (Letters of Credit), freight bill discounting, commodity trade finance, or correspondent-bank-backed USD clearing. EMIs cannot lawfully issue commercial documentary letters of credit without a partner bank; for high-value sulfur cargo settlements, a Tier-1 commercial bank account remains mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under Law 10/2010 and Banco de España Circular 7/2016, Spanish banks are required to identify the beneficial owners and directors of a Spanish SL. Physical presence of the founding director or a duly appointed legal representative (apoderado) with notarised and apostilled power of attorney is generally required by Tier-1 banks for initial account activation; however, qualified remote video identification using eIDAS-certified digital signatures and recognised authentication is increasingly accepted where the company has a Spanish NIF and the director’s identity document can be verified electronically. Non-resident directors without a Spanish NIF or with no European Economic Area residence will almost always be required to attend an in-person compliance interview at the bank's international banking centre in Madrid or Barcelona.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) not immediately determinable or layered corporate shareholders located in opaque jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date notarised and apostilled certificate of incorporation; register of share transfers; an individual tax-identification-number (NIF/NIE) for each natural-person UBO; a written control-chain narrative; certified group structure chart; residency evidence; affidavit confirming no nominee shareholders; supporting documents from the Spanish commercial registry (Registro Mercantil).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume commodity trade with non-EU counterparties and volatile invoice values, triggering enhanced due diligence for unusual transaction patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master sales contract (ISDA/ICS-style or commodity purchase agreement); commercial invoices for each cargo; certified bill of lading, shore tank receipt and certificate of quantity/quality; warehouse storage or vessel charter-party evidenced by a legally valid bill of lading; evidence of underlying physical freight and storage costs; customs export/import declarations (DUA) showing HS 2503/2802 codes for elemental sulfur / sulfur ore; bank references from prior operational accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to or from third-country jurisdictions appearing in sanctioned or high-risk lists, or use of shell corporate veils.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A sanctions-screening report from a recognised compliance provider (Dow Jones, Moody's, Refinitiv, or World-Check); clean criminal-record certificates and politically-exposed-person declarations for directors/UBOs; copies of passports and residence permits; beneficial-ownership registry certificates (Registro de Titularidades Reales) or equivalent; contracts and documentary proof of genuine physical movement of goods; justification of business rationale for each payment corridor; third-party due-diligence folders on suppliers and end-buyers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Automatic scrutiny of letters of credit and freight payments due to suspicious invoice discounting or unverified trade documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original letter of credit, SWIFT MT700/MT720 traffic with full narrative; compliant shipping documents (clean negotiable bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, insurance certificate under ICC Incoterms 2020); pre-shipment inspection certificate (such as SGS / Intertek for sulfur analysis); cargo draft survey report; proof of vessel identity and location via AIS tracking log for the charter; freight invoices from independent ship brokers; evidence of LC issuance bank acceptance and negotiation of proceeds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions into the Spanish SL must pass through a Spanish-resident bank account as SWIFT MT103 with a clean purpose code referencing 'equity capital subscription' or 'shareholder loan'. The sending bank must include the Spanish NIF of the SL, the share-purchase deed, and the certification of the share premium account if applicable. For non-EU remittances, the bank will file a Form D-4 declaration to the Investment Registry (Registro de Inversiones) of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business; if the injected amount exceeds €3,000,000, the investment must be declared on Form D-4 within one month of recording in the commercial registry (for statistical purposes). No prior authorisation is required unless the target activity triggers foreign investment screening under public order, security, or regulated sectors; dry-bulk mineral trading is outside those restricted sectors. All filings must be reconciled with the Banco de España foreign-transaction declaration system through the receiving bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement from the Spanish account is executed via SWIFT MT103 for direct bank transfers, MT202 for interbank clearing in correspondent currencies, and SWIFT MT700/MT720 for documentary letters of credit (import or export LCs). For euro-zone buyers, SEPA and TARGET2 are the primary clearing rails. For USD-denominated cargoes, the SL must clear through its bank’s American correspondent network (e.g., Bank of New York Mellon, J.P. Morgan, Citibank, or Bank of America) using SWIFT and CHIPS/wire protocols. Commercial LCs must be issued in conformity with ICC UCP 600 and ISP98 for standby arrangements; presentation of documents is to the issuing or confirming bank in Madrid/FPI is standard. All disbursements require the corresponding export declaration (DUA) or Intrastat filing and the Bank of Spain monthly transaction report when the threshold is met.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts (FX forwards) for lawful hedging of USD/EUR and other convertible pairs
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) on currencies without deliverability under Spanish/MiFID II authorisation
FX options and option combinations used solely for hedging underlying commercial exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts, including the beneficial ownership declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approve within six months after the financial year-end and file within one month after approval. For a calendar-year company, the usual filing deadline is 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure may be imposed after one year from the end of the filing period. Administrative fines generally range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000 and may reach EUR 300,000 for companies with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6 million, subject to statutory conditions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Form 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the usual filing window is 1 to 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties, late-payment interest, and collection surcharges may apply under the General Tax Law. Penalties depend on whether the return is filed voluntarily or after a tax authority notice and whether tax is payable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation in the annual accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the annual accounts within one month after approval. The declaration must reflect the current ultimate beneficial owner and any changes in ownership or control.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incorrect or omitted beneficial ownership information may cause filing rejection, registry closure consequences, and potential administrative or anti-money-laundering liability. Ownership and control changes should be documented and reported through the applicable corporate and registry channels without delay.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is generally mandatory where the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets of EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover of EUR 5.7 million, or an average workforce of 50 employees. Mandatory audit also applies in specified cases, including certain regulated, public-interest, group, subsidized, or court-ordered circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad, Spanish GAAP). IFRS is mandatory for consolidated accounts of listed groups and may apply in other regulated circumstances.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain does not generally require a separate standalone annual UBO return solely because shares were transferred. The Register of Members must be updated for share transfers, the transfer must be reflected in the annual beneficial ownership declaration filed with the annual accounts, and material changes in ownership or control must be updated through the applicable Mercantile Registry, notarial, and beneficial ownership information channels.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of contracts with the sole shareholder, where the SL is wholly owned by one shareholder

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 300-1,200 per year, depending on location and the scope of registered-office, mail-handling, and corporate-secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 1,500-5,000 for a small non-complex SL subject to statutory audit; fees increase with turnover, transactions, group reporting, inventory, and cross-border activity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for newly incorporated SL for the first two tax periods with a positive taxable base; additional R&D tax credits up to 42%; exemption or reduction for the sale of intellectual property; participation exemption for foreign-source dividends and capital gains; tax-loss carryforward limited to 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return) — AEAT Electronic Office (Sede Electrónica), using digital certificate or Cl@ve PIN.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days after the first six months following the end of the tax period; for a calendar-year entity, by 25 July of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Identification Number of the Spanish SL or its permanent establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the NIF assigned to the SL; non-resident shareholders do not file on this box unless the return is filed for a Spanish permanent establishment, in which case the PE's NIF is used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the fiscal year covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the SL's complete fiscal year; for a non-resident with a permanent establishment, use the PE's registered tax period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after adjusting accounting profit by non-deductible expenses, applying exemptions, and compensating prior tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Spanish resident SL, report worldwide taxable income; for a non-resident PE, report only income attributable to the Spanish PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 550 (Resultado de la autoliquidación / Cuota íntegra)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable or refundable after applying credits, deductions, instalment payments, and withholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the Spanish SL's full corporate tax liability; the non-resident status of shareholders has no direct effect on Box 550.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers LGT Article 27 surcharge (5% per month up to 20% of tax payable) plus late-payment interest; an unfiled return is penalized under Article 198 with a flat EUR 200 fine or EUR 10 per omitted box; incorrect or fraudulent understatement carries penalties of 50% to 150% of the tax amount under Article 191.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202 (Corporate Income Tax Instalment Payment) — AEAT Electronic Office.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December for calendar-year companies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Identification Number of the entity making the instalment payment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL itself files this form; non-resident owners have no direct filing obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year taxable base, adjusted for the chosen instalment method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Computed under Spanish domestic rules; treaty relief applicable to the final tax does not reduce quarterly instalments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory percentage applied to the base to calculate the instalment amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the applicable percentage for the SL; no allocation to foreign shareholders is made in this form.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted Modelo 202 carries the LGT Article 27 surcharge, late-payment interest, and an Article 198 penalty; underpayment is ultimately adjusted in the annual Modelo 200.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% for residents of EU/EEA states with effective exchange of information and for residents of treaty countries; 24% for non-residents from non-treaty jurisdictions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its country of residence, provide it to the paying Spanish company before distribution to apply the treaty withholding rate at source, or, if excess tax is withheld, file Form 210 (Impuesto sobre la Renta de No Residentes) with AEAT, attaching the TRC and supporting documentation, to claim a refund.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-resident WHT: 24% on royalties and interest paid to non-residents. Under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive, related-company payments may enjoy 0% withholding; treaty rates typically range from 0% to 10% for interest and 5% to 10% for royalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory when Spanish net turnover exceeds EUR 10 million; Master File mandatory when the multinational group's consolidated turnover reaches EUR 45 million; de minimis transaction thresholds apply (EUR 250,000 per related-party transaction type).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain is not a Caribbean-style ESR jurisdiction, but the OECD substance principle and the Spanish General Anti-Abuse Rule (Article 15 LGT) require actual management, employees, premises, and commercial risk in the Spanish SL. A pure conduit or shell entity will be re-characterized, treaty benefits denied, and profits reallocated to the place of genuine substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting sulfur ore trade revenues, issuing or using false purchase invoices, shifting profits to affiliated entities in zero-tax jurisdictions, or artificially inflating deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties under Article 305 Penal Code: imprisonment of 1 to 5 years, a fine of 2 to 6 times the amount evaded, and loss of public subsidies and tax benefits where the evaded amount exceeds EUR 120,000. Administrative penalty under LGT Article 191: 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who order, approve, or benefit from the scheme are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt under LGT Article 42; criminal conviction may result in disqualification from managing companies, asset seizure, and judicial travel bans while proceedings are pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Spanish SL with no real office, no employees, no management decisions, and no commercial substance, used solely to attach Spanish tax residency or treaty benefits to an international sulfur trading operation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish tax authorities can ignore the legal entity under substance-over-form and Article 15 LGT, deny treaty relief, reassess the income at shareholder level, and apply Article 206 concealment penalties of up to 150% of the reassessed tax, plus late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of an artificial conduit are jointly liable for the resulting tax assessment and penalties; if the shell is used to defraud Spanish revenue, criminal liability for tax evasion attaches personally, with imprisonment, civil restitution, and precautionary seizure or travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Purchasing elemental sulfur from related parties at supra-arm's-length prices, routing sales through related entities to reduce Spanish margin, or failing to file Master File/Local File above the EUR 10 million threshold without contemporaneous TP study.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT will adjust the taxable base to arm's length and charge late-payment interest; defective or missing TP documentation carries a fine under LGT Article 206 of up to EUR 5,000 per data deficiency; incorrect valuation producing a tax loss triggers a 15% penalty on the adjusted transaction value, escalating to 50%-150% if fraud is proven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the tax return or approve the non-arm's-length contracts are jointly and severally liable for the corrected tax and associated penalties; willful TP manipulation is prosecutable as tax fraud, exposing directors to imprisonment and forfeiture of assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering / Trade-Based Financing AML Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to conduct customer due diligence on Letter of Credit beneficiaries, overlooking sanctioned counterparts, or structuring large sulfur ore payments to avoid monitoring in high-risk corridors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 10/2010, serious infringements attract fines from EUR 60,001 to EUR 5,000,000 and possible suspension of operations; aggravated or repeated violations may lead to revocation of the tax licence and prohibition on acting as director for up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Compliance officers and managing directors may be personally fined up to EUR 60,000 for gross negligence; if the trade transactions form part of a criminal predatory scheme, Article 301 of the Penal Code provides imprisonment of 6 months to 6 years, asset freezing, and court-imposed restrictions on leaving Spain.
